records.text: A Lordaeron watchman posted in the same region as the sentries. In combat, he strikes, uses a shield, and may flee for help when badly hurt.
A Lordaeron sentry posted alongside the watchmen. In combat, the sentry uses a ranged shot.

A Durnholde sentry on guard, he passes idle time grumbling that quitting time cannot come soon enough and wondering about a vacation in Hearthglen. He has also heard that Blackmoore has been acting strangely.

A Durnholde rifleman in the guard, he passes idle time grumbling that quitting time cannot come soon enough and wondering about a vacation in Hearthglen. He has also heard that Blackmoore has been acting strangely.
The warden's idle chatter pairs unease about Blackmoore's strange behavior with thoughts of a Hearthglen vacation and impatience for quitting time.
A humanoid pit spectator.
The veteran's idle chatter pairs unease about Blackmoore's strange behavior with thoughts of a Hearthglen vacation and impatience for quitting time.

Young Thrall is imprisoned beneath Durnholde Keep. He dreams of his people overthrowing their oppressors, breaking their bonds and rising together as the orcish Horde. He hopes to escape and free Taretha, whose kindness he promises never to forget. He is alarmed by the magic affecting her. If helped to escape, he credits Taretha’s friends and promises to seek out and reward those helping him when he has the means.
A Tarren Mill guardsman, he serves among the settlement's armed defenders. In combat he can answer threats with Mortal Strike and Shield Charge.
A Tarren Mill protector, he serves among the settlement's armed defenders. In combat he can answer threats with Cleave.

A Tarren Mill lookout, he watches the disturbance surrounding Thrall's escape. His warnings track movement at the barn and a startled horse, then report Thrall trapped in the chapel; he believes Thrall cannot escape there.
An Orc Prisoner held in the Tarren Mill area, he complains of feeling unwell and being hungry and thirsty. His brief remarks present the shared experience of a captive awaiting food and water.
A Tarren Mill peasant who works among the apple trees, sometimes grumbling as he works. When asked, the peasant readily says there are plenty of apples and gives permission to take one.

Tarren Mill's horsehand cares for Bessy, arranging walks for her and worrying when she is cooped up or hungry. He asks his old friend Benjamin for an apple for her, showing familiar ties to both the horse and the orchard's keeper.
Monica is identified as an innkeeper.
A Tarren Mill horse that whinnies happily and can follow the nearby Horsehand when directed.
Jay Lemieux is a child at play, calling “Tag! You’re it!” to keep a game of tag moving.
Julie Honeywell asks to join in, then declares boys gross. Her brief remarks suggest someone eager for company but quick to dismiss the boys around her.

The Tarren Mill Fisherman wonders whether they will see Ol’ Sooty, dreads pulling up another of Reggy’s boots, and is relieved when Bertha is not around. His talk gives him an easy, locally minded voice, mixing curiosity, annoyance, and relief.
The Aged Dalaran Wizard offers goods for sale and casts Frost Armor while out of combat. His role is practical: an older mage serving customers and keeping a protective spell ready.
A Dalaran sorceress.
Thomas Yance is a travelling salesman who offers goods and repairs. His trade is practical and mobile, with repair service adding a useful role alongside selling supplies.
A humanoid pit announcer.

Erozion is a temporal guardian working to preserve the events that led to Thrall’s escape from Durnholde. He arranges the diversion, then explains that Thrall’s memory must be restored to its original course and that Taretha’s fate cannot be changed.
Brazen is Erozion’s flight companion, offering to carry travelers to Durnholde. Brazen cautions that Erozion’s incendiary bombs should be obtained before the journey.
A Durnholde armorer stationed in the keep, he reacts to a disturbance with a startled protest and a call for guards.
The Durnholde Cook works as a cook in the keep.

Taretha is being held by an unfamiliar wizard whose strange talk of time leaves her asking her friends to find him and release her. When she reunites with Thrall, she welcomes his escape, rejects the claim that he is a monster, and thanks those helping her. Her words show warmth toward Thrall and gratitude to her rescuers.

Hal McAllister answers Nat directly and meets Nat's claims with disbelief, calling one a whopper and another impossible. He also says he worries about Nat, giving their exchange a note of concern alongside his skepticism.

Nat Pagle recalls a recurring strange dream in which undead destroy Tarren Mill and it becomes Southshore’s enemy. He also starts recounting a king’s murder after a false show of friendliness, and remembers Foror and Tigule as loud-mouthed ruffians.

Commander Mograine has carried an object for ten years, since Blackrock Spire, and describes it as a manifestation of shadow and void. In a gathering about Lordaeron’s fate, he urges preparation for an undead holocaust, presses to understand the object, then asks that its existence remain secret.

Isillien takes part in Mograine’s discussion of an evil artifact and insists it should be destroyed. He challenges Mograine directly, then notices that Mograine’s hand has healed and names the Ashbringer.
Abbendis reacts with alarm at the Light and the Ashbringer.

Fairbanks watches the Ashbringer change: he asks whether it is getting lighter and remarks that its coloration is changing, then names the blade in wonder. His brief response marks him as a witness to the weapon’s transformation.
Tirion Fordring warns that the kingdom is ill-prepared for an assault by forces he says he has fought himself. His remarks express disbelief and draw attention to the Ashbringer.

Kel’Thuzad bears the title “The Kirin Tor” but dismisses their judgment as archaic. He urges Helcular to keep his voice down around strangers and presents necromancy as a gift he has the power to bestow. He rebukes Helcular as neither Kirin Tor nor a necromancer, withholds matters he considers none of Helcular’s concern and tells him to wait. Confident in his power, he combines secrecy with contempt for his peers’ objections.

Captain Sanders talks with Ed about his ship and hidden treasure, boasting about the small, eccentric contents he has secured, including a white shirt and an enormous bag sized for eight apples. His repeated hiccups and talk of getting another drink place the exchange in a drunken pirate performance.
In a brief exchange addressed to Mograine, Arcanist Doan asks what Mograine proposes and then refers to the Ashbringer.

Helcular is shown seeking instruction in necromancy from Kel'Thuzad. He asks what the Kirin Tor think of necromancy, then urges Kel'Thuzad to teach him everything he knows. The exchange presents him as an aspiring student.
Nathanos Marris is a human ranger lord, a disciple of Sylvanas Windrunner and the only human allowed to train under the high elves.
Stalvan Mistmantle is a humanoid.
A humanoid named Sally Whitemane.
A humanoid named Renault Mograine.
A humanoid named Little Jimmy Vishas.
A humanoid named Herod the Bully.
Taelan is a named humanoid.

Caretaker Smithers resents being ordered around and made to do farm work, grumbling that he hopes the place becomes a graveyard. His recorded routine has him gathering vegetables, digging, moving rocks, and taking breaks.

Bartolo Ginsetti is a shameless self-promoter who boasts about his physique and greatness. He dreams of making a fortune from his cloaks and having the Ginsetti name coveted as far as Ironforge; he even warns visitors to keep their hands off his cloak.
Farmer Kent is a farmer.
Phin Odelic bears the designation “The Kirin Tor.”
Jonathan Revah is enthusiastic about building a tower halfway between Tarren Mill and Southshore, seeing it as a symbol of friendship and brotherhood between the towns.
Henry Maleb bears the title of magistrate.
Jerry Carter admires the tower project and exclaims to Jonathan that it is glorious.
Barkeep Kelly is a bartender who offers goods to browse.
Chef Jessen forcefully demands quiet in the bar, threatening to wield his rolling pin and cleaver, and snaps at Mograine as “mister fancy britches.”
A humanoid named Bilger the Straight-laced.
A humanoid named Raleigh the True.

Captain Edward Hanes is a ship captain whose exchanges with Sanders turn to Sanders’s chest and the ships beside Hanes’s frigate. Hanes is taken aback by the treasure, then speaks excitedly of sailing a ship around the world.
Frances Lin is a barmaid who offers service with a direct “What’ll it be?” and later asks about more grog.

Zixil, an aspiring merchant, is repairing a machine so he can travel the roads without fear of bandits. He hopes to sell machines to other goblins, grow rich, and make his name by cornering the market; his talk is openly ambitious.
Overwatch Mark 0 is a mechanical protector.

A Kirin Tor mage is present in the Caverns of Time's Old Hillsbrad setting, where several level 47 mages of this type are recorded. The supplied records establish no specific duty or personal history.
A Hillsbrad peasant is found in the Old Hillsbrad setting. Records place multiple level 10–12 peasants in the area, but give no individual service or personal story.
A Hillsbrad citizen appears in the Old Hillsbrad setting. Several citizens of this type are recorded there, with levels ranging from 12 to 32; no individual role is supplied.

This Hillsbrad citizen complains that reconstruction taxes are straining ordinary people and doubts King Terenas's judgment. In conversation, the citizen repeats hearsay that Prince Arthas neglects state affairs while pursuing Jaina Proudmoore, then agrees that Uther is a hero.

This Hillsbrad citizen discusses Terenas as changed by the war and hopes Arthas will become a fine king, while repeating reports that he is training as a paladin under Uther's guidance. The citizen also passes along rumors about Lieutenant Blackmoore's formidable new gladiator.
This Hillsbrad citizen has seen Blackmoore's orc gladiator fight and regrets losing a week's wages betting against him. The citizen fears what might happen if the powerful fighter ever escaped.
A humanoid called Beggar.
Hillsbrad farmers are local inhabitants of the Old Hillsbrad area.
A horse is a local presence in the Old Hillsbrad area.
Natasha Morris is a named local figure in the Old Hillsbrad area.
A humanoid named Victor.
A humanoid named Alex.
A humanoid named Harvey.
A humanoid named Phil.
A humanoid named Hugh.
Don Carlos is a named, high-ranking combatant. He fights with a ranged weapon, nets, and scatter shots; upon dying, he says, “Im... possible...”

place_records.text: You are in Old Hillsbrad Foothills, a stretch of Hillsbrad from another time, reached from Tanaris. Epoch Hunter, Captain Skarloc and Lieutenant Drake are its masters, and Durnholde sentries keep watch over it. Young Thrall is imprisoned beneath Durnholde Keep, and the Infinite hold Taretha captive at Tarren Mill.

You are in Tarren Mill, a settlement with an inn kept by Innkeeper Monica. A peasant works among the apple trees and says there are plenty of apples to take. A horsehand cares for a horse named Bessy, while Tarren Mill lookouts, protectors and guardsmen stand guard alongside Lordaeron watchmen.

You are in Southshore, where Nat Pagle recalls a recurring dream in which undead destroy Tarren Mill and Tarren Mill becomes Southshore's enemy. Hal McAllister meets Nat's claims with disbelief, though he says he worries about Nat. Commander Mograine warns of an undead holocaust and urges preparation, describing an object he has carried for ten years, since Blackrock Spire, as a manifestation of shadow and void.
You are in Durnholde Keep, where Durnholde sentries, wardens, veterans, armorers and cooks are all posted. An orc prisoner complains of feeling unwell, hungry and thirsty.
